observations.explanation: The paper describes a multi-stage flow that repeatedly runs and fixes code against public and AI-generated tests, with problem reflection and test generation as part of preprocessing (PDF pp. 1, 3–4).
Table 1 reports gains on both validation and test splits for DeepSeek-33B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4; it also gives GPT-4 validation pass@5 as 19% versus 44% (PDF p. 7).

The evaluation uses 107 validation problems and 165 test problems, and the paper’s reported experiments are on CodeContests. The stated concern about confidence in generalization beyond this benchmark is a reasonable limitation (PDF p. 3).

The paper notes that prior systems did not release reproducible end-to-end solutions and identifies evaluation subtleties, including multiple solutions, tolerances, and timeouts. These caveats support qualifying cross-system comparisons, while the paper still reports superiority (PDF p. 7).
